questions.stem: In an experiment to measure specific heat capacity, why is it important to insulate the container?

options.text: To minimise heat loss to the surroundings, improving accuracy
To increase the mass of the substance
To make the substance heat up faster

questions.explanation: Insulating the container reduces heat loss to the surroundings. If heat escapes, the measured temperature rise will be less than expected, making the calculated specific heat capacity appear too high. Good insulation improves the accuracy of the result.
